expected_core_reactions.description: EntC (isochorismate synthase, EC 5.4.4.2) isomerises chorismate to isochorismate. The paper states the reaction is magnesium-dependent and highly reversible.
expected_core_reactions.quote: the EntC‐catalyzed isomerization of chorismate to isochorismate has a relatively low enthalpy change
expected_core_reactions.rationale: First step of the requested pathway; substrate, product, enzyme and EC number are all stated, and the reaction is measured directly by ITC.

expected_core_reactions.description: The N-terminal isochorismatase (IC) domain of EntB (EC 3.3.2.1) hydrolyses isochorismate to 2,3-dihydro-2,3-dihydroxybenzoate (2,3-diDHB) and pyruvate.
expected_core_reactions.quote: isochorismate is converted to 2,3‐dihydro‐2,3‐dihydroxybenzoate (2,3‐diDHB) and pyruvate by EntB isochorismatase activity
expected_core_reactions.rationale: Explicitly asserted with both products named; it is the reaction the entire paper measures, and the paper calls it the committed step of the pathway.

expected_core_reactions.description: EntA (2,3-dihydro-2,3-dihydroxybenzoate dehydrogenase, EC 1.3.1.28) oxidises 2,3-diDHB to 2,3-dihydroxybenzoic acid (2,3-DHB), the third and last reaction of the DHB synthetic arm.
expected_core_reactions.quote: the biosynthetic intermediate 2,3‐DHB is produced from chorismate by sequential reactions catalyzed by three enzymes: (i) EntC (isochorismate synthase; EC 5.4.4.2), (ii) the N‐terminal isochorismatase (IC) domain of EntB (EC 3.3.2.1), and (iii) EntA (2,3‐dihydro‐2,3‐dihydroxybenzoate dehydrogenase; EC 1.3.1.28)
expected_core_reactions.rationale: The paper asserts that these three enzymes acting sequentially produce 2,3-DHB from chorismate and names EntA's activity as 2,3-dihydro-2,3-dihydroxybenzoate dehydrogenase, which fixes both sides; but unlike R1 and R2 it never writes this single transformation out, hence medium not high. NOTE: the paper never names a cofactor (no NAD+) for this dehydrogenase.

expected_core_reactions.description: EntD phosphopantetheinylates the aryl carrier protein (ArCP) domain of apo-EntB at Ser 245, converting apo-EntB to holo-EntB. A protein modification, not a metabolite conversion.
expected_core_reactions.quote: the ArCP domain of apo ‐EntB itself must be phosphopantetheinylated at Ser 245 by the accessory enzyme EntD to form holo ‐EntB
expected_core_reactions.rationale: An explicitly asserted, enzyme-catalysed, site-specific transformation that the paper states is required for the pathway to run; medium because it modifies a protein rather than converting a small-molecule intermediate, and the phosphopantetheine donor (coenzyme A) is never named.

expected_core_reactions.description: EntE (2,3-dihydroxybenzoyl-AMP ligase, EC 6.2.1.71) adenylates 2,3-DHB in an ATP-dependent reaction, giving the activated acyl-adenylate.
expected_core_reactions.quote: 2,3‐DHB is adenylated by EntE (2,3‐dihydroxybenzoyl‐AMP ligase; EC 6.2.1.71) in an ATP‐dependent reaction
expected_core_reactions.rationale: The transformation and its ATP dependence are stated plainly and this is the first step of the paper's declared second stage. CAVEAT: the product 2,3-dihydroxybenzoyl-AMP is named only inside the enzyme's own systematic name, never as a free intermediate; pyrophosphate is never mentioned.

expected_core_reactions.description: The adenylated 2,3-DHB is covalently attached to the ArCP domain of holo-EntB (loading of the carrier protein).
expected_core_reactions.quote: in an ATP‐dependent reaction in order to facilitate its covalent attachment to the aryl carrier protein (ArCP) domain of EntB
expected_core_reactions.rationale: The paper asserts that adenylation exists in order to achieve covalent attachment of 2,3-DHB to the EntB ArCP domain; medium because the paper never states the loading step as its own catalysed reaction and does not name the thioester product.

expected_core_reactions.description: The EntB C-terminal ArCP domain transfers the phosphopantetheinylated 2,3-DHB onto phosphopantetheinylated (holo-) EntF.
expected_core_reactions.quote: then transfers phosphopantetheinylated 2,3‐DHB to EntF via the EntB C‐terminal aryl carrier protein (ArCP) domain
expected_core_reactions.rationale: Asserted twice (abstract and introduction) as one of EntB's two catalytic functions; medium because it is a carrier-to-carrier transfer whose product is never named as a discrete species.

expected_core_reactions.description: EntF (enterobactin synthase) performs three cycles of condensation of the activated 2,3-DHB with L-serine through non-ribosomal peptide bond formation, then cyclises and releases the product, enterobactin: three 2,3-DHB subunits on a triserine trilactone core.
expected_core_reactions.quote: Enterobactin production from activated 2,3‐DHB then involves three EntF‐catalyzed cycles of condensation with L‐serine via the formation of non‐ribosomal peptide bonds followed by cyclization and product release
expected_core_reactions.rationale: The terminal assembly of the requested pathway, with both substrates, the catalyst and the product named; kept as one entry because the paper describes condensation, cyclization and release as one EntF-catalysed sequence and never separates their chemistry.

expected_major_subprocesses.name: the DHB synthetic arm: production of 2,3-DHB from chorismate (first stage)
aliases: DHB synthetic arm of the pathway
expected_major_subprocesses.kind_rationale: Three sequential enzymatic conversions carry chorismate through isochorismate and 2,3-diDHB to 2,3-DHB, all of them substrate-to-product transformations.
expected_major_subprocesses.quote: In Escherichia coli , enterobactin is synthesized in the cytoplasm in two stages. In the first stage (Figure 1 ), the biosynthetic intermediate 2,3‐DHB is produced from chorismate by sequential reactions catalyzed by three enzymes
expected_major_subprocesses.rationale: The paper explicitly divides enterobactin biosynthesis into two stages and names this one, giving all three of its reactions with EC numbers.

expected_major_subprocesses.name: second stage: activation of 2,3-DHB and NRPS assembly of enterobactin
aliases: the second stage of the pathway
expected_major_subprocesses.kind_rationale: ATP-dependent activation, covalent loading onto the carrier protein, transfer to EntF and three condensation cycles with L-serine are all conversions of matter ending in enterobactin.
expected_major_subprocesses.quote: In the second stage of the pathway, 2,3‐DHB is adenylated by EntE
expected_major_subprocesses.rationale: The paper's own second named stage, running from ATP-dependent activation of 2,3-DHB through carrier-protein loading to EntF-catalysed condensation and cyclization.

expected_major_subprocesses.name: phosphopantetheinylation (priming) of the EntB aryl carrier protein domain by EntD
expected_major_subprocesses.kind_rationale: EntD covalently attaches a phosphopantetheine arm to Ser 245 of EntB, so apo-EntB becomes holo-EntB: a chemical modification of matter and a maturation step, not a control on how much flux passes through the pathway.
expected_major_subprocesses.quote: In order to deliver 2,3‐DHB to holo ‐EntF, the ArCP domain of apo ‐EntB itself must be phosphopantetheinylated at Ser 245 by the accessory enzyme EntD to form holo ‐EntB.
expected_major_subprocesses.rationale: The paper treats this as a required constituent step of the pathway (EntD is one of the ent gene products it lists), but it primes a protein rather than transforming a pathway metabolite.

expected_major_subprocesses.name: feedback regulation of enterobactin biosynthesis by 2,3-DHB
aliases: competitive inhibition of EntB isochorismatase by 2,3-DHB
expected_major_subprocesses.kind_rationale: The paper is explicit that 2,3-DHB is neither a substrate nor a product of EntB here; the stage is competitive inhibition that lowers flux through the committed step, so its whole content is control rather than chemistry.
expected_major_subprocesses.quote: these in vitro observations suggest that 2,3‐DHB may play a biological role as a negative feedback regulator of enterobactin biosynthesis via direct inhibition of EntB following accumulation of sufficient intracellular iron
expected_major_subprocesses.rationale: This is the paper's actual finding and it is explicitly framed as regulation OF enterobactin biosynthesis, but it is a regulatory mechanism and groups no chemical transformation of its own; recorded with no reaction ids and low confidence for that reason.

important_participants.name: chorismate
important_participants.quote: the EntC‐catalyzed isomerization of chorismate to isochorismate
important_participants.note: The entry metabolite of the pathway; R1 is not the isochorismate synthase reaction without it.

important_participants.name: isochorismate
important_participants.quote: confirmed that EntB was required to drive the EntC reaction toward isochorismate formation
important_participants.note: Product of R1 and substrate of R2; the channelled intermediate the paper's whole kinetic argument turns on.

important_participants.name: 2,3-dihydro-2,3-dihydroxybenzoate
important_participants.quote: isochorismate is converted to 2,3‐dihydro‐2,3‐dihydroxybenzoate (2,3‐diDHB) and pyruvate
important_participants.note: Product of the EntB isochorismatase reaction and the substrate that gives EntA its systematic name.

important_participants.name: pyruvate
important_participants.quote: 2,3‐dihydro‐2,3‐dihydroxybenzoate (2,3‐diDHB) and pyruvate by EntB isochorismatase activity
important_participants.note: The co-product released by isochorismatase hydrolysis. Arguably a currency metabolite, but here it is one of the two named products of R2 and the species the coupled assay actually detects.

important_participants.name: 2,3-dihydroxybenzoic acid
important_participants.quote: The enterobactin biosynthetic intermediate 2,3‐dihydroxybenzoic acid is a competitive inhibitor of the Escherichia coli isochorismatase EntB
important_participants.note: The molecule the paper is about. Three roles in this paper: pathway intermediate, EntE substrate, and competitive inhibitor of EntB, which the paper is explicit is neither a substrate nor a product of EntB.

important_participants.name: ATP
important_participants.note: Adenylation is not identifiable as adenylation without ATP; it also fixes the direction of R5 toward the activated acyl-adenylate.

important_participants.name: L-serine
important_participants.quote: three EntF‐catalyzed cycles of condensation with L‐serine via the formation of non‐ribosomal peptide bonds
important_participants.note: Supplies the triserine trilactone core; without it R8 is not enterobactin assembly.

important_participants.name: enterobactin
important_participants.quote: Enterobactin is a catecholate siderophore with extraordinarily high affinity for ferric iron
important_participants.note: The end product of the requested pathway. Its composition is stated: three 2,3-DHB subunits connected via a triserine trilactone core.

important_participants.name: holo-EntB
important_participants.quote: must be phosphopantetheinylated at Ser 245 by the accessory enzyme EntD to form holo ‐EntB
important_participants.note: The phosphopantetheinylated state of EntB. It is a state of one polypeptide, not a separate protein; without the apo/holo distinction the carrier-loading steps cannot be told apart.

secondary_participants.name: Mg2+
secondary_participants.quote: confirming that the observed heats were indeed due to magnesium‐dependent EntC enzymatic activity
secondary_participants.note: Required for EntC activity; removing it abolished the ITC signal. A metal cofactor, not a pathway metabolite.

secondary_participants.name: water
secondary_participants.quote: catalyzes hydrolysis of isochorismate via its N‐terminal isochorismatase (IC) domain
secondary_participants.note: Never named as a species; its participation is implied only by the word hydrolysis. Recorded here so it is not mistaken for an omitted important substrate.

secondary_participants.name: EntD
secondary_participants.note: The paper's own word is accessory. EntD is the CATALYST of R4 and merely ancillary to everything downstream; recorded in both lists deliberately (see uncertainties).

secondary_participants.name: 2,3-dihydroxybenzoic acid
secondary_participants.quote: 2,3‐DHB is a competitive inhibitor of apo ‐EntB isochorismatase activity
secondary_participants.note: Same molecule as the important participant above. In R2 it is neither substrate nor product but a competitive inhibitor, i.e. a regulator. Deliberate dual listing per the brief's rule.

secondary_participants.name: Fur
secondary_participants.quote: is controlled by the protein Ferric Uptake Regulator (Fur)
secondary_participants.note: Transcriptional repressor of the ent genes under iron-replete conditions. Regulates expression, catalyses no step.

secondary_participants.name: ferric iron
secondary_participants.quote: Following secretion, enterobactin chelates extracellular ferric iron
secondary_participants.note: The purpose of the pathway's product, but chelation happens extracellularly after secretion and is not a biosynthetic step.

uncertainties: R3 (EntA) is medium, not high, because the paper never writes that transformation out as its own sentence. It is fixed by two statements taken together: that the three named enzymes acting sequentially produce 2,3-DHB from chorismate, and that EntA's systematic name is 2,3-dihydro-2,3-dihydroxybenzoate dehydrogenase. A reviewer who requires a single explicit sentence per reaction would downgrade R3 to low.

R3 has NO cofactor listed. NAD+ is the textbook cofactor of EC 1.3.1.28 but this paper never mentions it, and the only NAD species in the file (NADH/NAD+) belong to the LDH coupled-assay readout. Adding NAD+ here would be importing from outside the paper.

R5's product, 2,3-dihydroxybenzoyl-AMP, is named ONLY inside EntE's systematic name and never as a free intermediate. Pyrophosphate is never mentioned. The transformation itself is asserted unambiguously, so I kept R5 at high, but the product naming is weaker than the reaction.

R6 and R7 are the two carrier-protein transfer steps (loading onto the EntB ArCP domain, then delivery to holo-EntF). Both are asserted, but as purposes and mechanisms rather than as separately catalysed reactions, and neither thioester species is named. Both are medium. A reviewer could reasonably merge R6 into R5, or merge R6 and R7 into R8.

R8 bundles three condensation cycles plus cyclization plus product release into one reaction, because the paper describes them as one EntF-catalysed sequence and gives no separate chemistry for the cyclization. Splitting it would require detail the paper does not supply.

R4 (EntD phosphopantetheinylation) is a PROTEIN modification, not a metabolite conversion. I included it because the paper states it is required for the pathway to run and EntD is one of the ent gene products, but a consumer that expects only small-molecule conversions should expect to filter it. The phosphopantetheine donor (coenzyme A) is never named.

2,3-DHB IS DELIBERATELY LISTED TWICE: as an important participant (central_to_pathway_scope; it is the pathway intermediate and EntE's substrate) and as a secondary participant of class regulator for R2, where the paper is explicit that it is neither a substrate nor a product of EntB but a competitive inhibitor. This is the brief's rule about a molecule being important in one reaction and secondary in another, not a contradiction.
EntD IS ALSO LISTED TWICE, as the catalyst of R4 and as an ancillary_protein for the downstream steps; the paper's own word for it is accessory enzyme.

Pyruvate was the closest call among the participants. It is a currency metabolite in general, which argues for secondary, but here it is one of the two explicitly named products of R2 and the species the coupled assay detects, so I made it important. A reviewer could move it.
S4 (feedback regulation) is regulation, not chemistry, and carries no reaction ids; low confidence for the same reason as the equivalent entry in PMC12856317.

EntC-EntB isochorismate channeling and the hypothesised EntCBAE multienzyme complex are a real and prominent part of this paper, but they are a mechanism for metabolite flux rather than a stage of the pathway, so I did NOT create a subprocess for them. Flagged here in case a reviewer wants it recorded.

CROSS-PAPER DISCIPLINE: PMC12452463 is the other enterobactin paper in my set. Nothing was carried between them in either direction. Every entry above rests on a quote from THIS paper's own full_text.
